'''''Pentanema salicinum''''' (common name '''Irish fleabane''' (UK)<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> or '''willowleaf yellowhead''') is a plant species in the family [[Asteraceae]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pentanema salicinum (L.) D.Gut.Larr., Santos-Vicente, Anderb., E.Rico & M.M.Mart.Ort. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:77178422-1 |access-date=2022-07-02 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref> It is found across Eurasia from Portugal to Japan. It has been reported growing in the wild in a few scattered locations in North America but it has not become widely established there.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://eol.org/pages/468073/entries/38775794/overview|title=Encyclopedia of Life, ''Inula salicina''|accessdate=Mar 10, 2012|format=}}</ref><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=inula+salicina Altervista Flora Italiana, ''Inula salicina'' L.]</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=200024067 Flora of North America, Inula salicina Linnaeus, 1753. ]</ref><ref name=tabby>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200024067 Flora of China, ''Inula salicina'' Linnaeus, 1753.  <big>柳叶旋覆花</big> liu ye xuan fu hua ]</ref>

==Taxonomy==
[[File:Bombus lapidarius - Inula salicina - Valingu.jpg|thumb|Pollination by red-tailed bumblebee]]
''Pentanema salicinum'' was first described by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1753. It is known from a variety of common names including willowleaf yellowhead, '''Irish fleabane''' and '''willow-leaved Inula'''. Since its initial description it has also been ascribed a variety of Latin names, all of which are now regarded as synonyms and probably reflecting the still uncertain taxonomy of the genus, it being regarded as possibly [[paraphyletic]].

==Distribution==
''Pentanema salicinum'' is to be found extensively across mainland western Europe, from Spain through France, [[Benelux]], Germany, Poland, Denmark and southern [[Scandinavia]]. It only has a very restricted distribution is the [[British Isles]], being confined to a small area of south central Ireland, around [[Lough Derg (Shannon)|Lough Derg]] in north [[County Tipperary]] and south-east [[County Galway]]. Indeed, it is now reported<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.botanicgardens.ie/conserve/inula.htm|title= Irish Botanic Gardens report on conservation program|accessdate=14 March 2012}}</ref> that it can only be found at a single locality, having been eliminated from former sites through human activity.  The species has become a flagship species and a focus for conservation efforts, with a co-ordinated program to reintroduce the plant already well underway. The plant is regarded a member of the [[Lusitanian flora]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishwildflowers.ie/lusitanian.html|title= Brief description of Lusitanian flora|accessdate=14 March 2012}}</ref> in that it is a member of a group of plants that are specific to south west [[Ireland]], are not found in the rest of the British Isles and are plants that are more normally seen in the Mediterranean. It is not known how this group of plants became established in Ireland, but it is likely to have been in the last 10,000 years since the end of the last [[ice age]].

==Description==
''Pentanema salicinum'' is an upright herb, {{convert|20|-|80|cm}} in height, with a thin stem, narrow, elongate, alternate, stemless leaves, which with the stem are roughly haired. The flower heads are carried singly at the top of the stem, are {{convert|2.5|-|4|cm}} in diameter. Each head contains 35-70 yellow ray flowers containing 100-250 yellow disc flowers.<ref name=tabby/>
